heading: INT. CABLE CAR - HIGH ALPINE SPAN - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CABLE CAR - HIGH ALPINE SPAN - NIGHT
A glass gondola hanging motionless over a black gorge.
Two benches face each other.
The cable creaks.
Wind howls.
A single emergency lamp glows orange.
LENA VASSILIOU, 30s, in a wool coat, sits on the downhill bench, one hand gripping the rail, the other pressed flat on a leather briefcase in her lap.
Across from her sits MILOS FERRANTE-OKORO, 40s, in an overcoat, knees bouncing, a thin smile on his face.
Neither has spoken since the car stopped.
Lena stares at the cable.
Milos stares at the briefcase.
It's a long way down, Lena.
units.name: MILOS

units.text: I know how far it is, Milos.
units.name: LENA

units.text: He reaches for the briefcase.
She pulls it back.
He stops with his hand halfway, and then leans back with elaborate calm and crosses his legs.
The gondola sways.
Lena shifts her grip.
A button on his coat catches the lamp and flashes.
Milos looks out the window, hums three bars of something, and glances at her again.
Lena watches his hands.
His fingers drum on his knee, one, two, one, two.
She counts the beat.
They'll restart the motor soon.
units.name: LENA

units.text: They'll restart it when I tell them.
units.name: MILOS

units.text: You can't tell them from here.
units.name: LENA

units.text: Can't I?
units.name: MILOS

units.text: He lifts his sleeve and taps his watch.
A tiny red light blinks on its face.
Lena goes still.
How long?
units.name: LENA

units.text: Ten minutes, Lena.
units.name: MILOS

units.text: Then you'd better take the case.
units.name: LENA

units.text: She lifts it and holds it out across the gap.
Milos looks at it for a long time, then at her, then at the case.
He does not take it.
